paras: The shooting of Dave Martin was the wounding of a Black man by a policeman at Peak's Station, near Alston, South Carolina, during the Christmas holidays of 1881. Martin was first reported killed while "resisting a policeman," but a later notice in the same Winnsboro paper said he was alive and expected to recover.

During the Christmas season, the policeman at Peak's Station shot Martin, whom the Winnsboro paper described as "colored." According to the first report, the man had been "resisting a policeman" when he was killed, though the paper added that "No particulars are given." Neither item names the policeman or says what led to the encounter, and the claim of resistance appears only in that first, unsourced account.

Three weeks later the paper corrected itself, stating that Martin "is not dead, as has been stated, but is now in a fair way to recover." No report of an arrest, inquiry or charge against the policeman appears in the coverage.

The Fairfield News and Herald of Winnsboro carried the only known reports, two one-sentence items in its local briefs column on 4 and 25 January 1882. The first item did not name the victim and passed on the account that he was resisting the officer; the second named him as Dave Martin and corrected only the report of his death. Both items ran without a headline or comment, set among notices of advertisements, church news and the weather.

The two reports disagree on the outcome: the 4 January item said the man was killed, while the 25 January item said he survived. The later notice explicitly corrected the earlier one, which had itself been presented as hearsay ("It is reported").
